Jump Game: can you reach the last index?
Track the farthest index you can reach so far. If the loop ever passes it, you are stuck. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Jump Game II: minimum number of jumps
This is BFS by levels without a queue. Each level is the range you can reach with jumps jumps. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Gas Station: find the starting station for a full circuit
If the total gas is at least the total cost, a solution exists. When the tank goes negative, every station from start to i fails as a starting point, so restart at i + 1. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Merge Intervals
Sort by start. Each interval either extends the last merged interval or starts a new one. O(n log n) time, O(n) for the output.
Insert Interval into a sorted, non-overlapping list
Three phases: copy the intervals before the new one, merge the ones that overlap it, then copy the rest. The input is already sorted, so this runs in O(n).
Non-overlapping Intervals: fewest removals
This is classic activity selection. Keeping the interval that ends earliest leaves the most room for the rest. O(n log n).
Meeting Rooms I: can one person attend every meeting?
After sorting by start, an overlap can only happen between neighbours. O(n log n).
Meeting Rooms II: minimum number of rooms
The heap holds one end time per room in use. Its size at the end is the answer. O(n log n). Another way: sort the starts and ends separately and sweep with two pointers.
Partition Labels
Record the last index of each character. Keep extending the current part's end, and cut when i reaches it. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Assign Cookies and Task Scheduler

Cookies: give each child the smallest cookie that works, O(n log n). Scheduler: the most frequent task sets the frame count. If the other tasks overflow the idle slots, the answer is just tasks.length. O(n).
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II (unlimited transactions)
Any rising run's total gain equals the sum of its daily gains, so collecting every positive difference is optimal. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Lemonade Change
Greedy choice: give back the larger bill first, because $5 bills are more flexible for future change. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons

Sort by end and shoot at the earliest end; that arrow pops every balloon starting at or before it. It is the counterpart of Non-overlapping Intervals (answer = n − removals). Integer.compare avoids overflow when values reach ±2³¹. O(n log n).
Boats to Save People (max 2 per boat, weight limit)
The heaviest person must take a boat; pairing them with the lightest is never worse than any other pairing. Sort plus two pointers: O(n log n).
Hand of Straights (split into groups of consecutive cards)
The smallest remaining card can only be the start of a group, which forces the choice. O(n log n) with a TreeMap. Same problem as "Divide Array in Sets of K Consecutive Numbers".
Valid Parenthesis String ('*' can be '(', ')' or empty)

Track the minimum and maximum number of unmatched '(' that are possible. Fail if even the maximum drops below 0; succeed if the minimum can reach 0. O(n) time, O(1) space, much simpler than the DP or two-stack approaches.
Interval List Intersections
Both lists are sorted and disjoint. The overlap of two intervals is [max start, min end]; then advance whichever ends first, because it cannot overlap anything later. O(m + n).
Candy (higher rating than a neighbour gets more candy)

Two passes: left-to-right enforces the rule against the left neighbour, right-to-left against the right one, and max keeps both satisfied. O(n) time, O(n) space. The "two-pass" idea also appears in Trapping Rain Water and Product Except Self.
Greedy vs dynamic programming: how do you know greedy is safe?

| Greedy | Dynamic programming
Decision | Take the locally best choice, never revisit | Try every choice, keep the best per state
Correct when | An exchange argument shows the greedy choice can be in some optimal answer | Optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems
Time | Often O(n log n) (sort) or O(n) | States × transitions, e.g. O(n · amount)
Coin change, coins {1, 3, 4}, amount 6 | 4 + 1 + 1 = 3 coins (wrong) | 3 + 3 = 2 coins (right)
Coin change, coins {1, 5, 10, 25} | Correct (canonical coin system) | Correct, but slower
Rule of thumb: try to break the greedy rule with a small counterexample. If you cannot, and you can explain why swapping in the greedy choice never hurts, use greedy; otherwise use DP.
Intervals: sort by start vs sort by end

| Sort by start | Sort by end
Goal | Combine or walk intervals in time order | Keep as many non-overlapping intervals as possible
Problems | Merge Intervals, Insert Interval, Meeting Rooms I/II | Non-overlapping Intervals, Minimum Arrows, activity selection
Why | Overlaps become neighbours | Ending earliest leaves the most room for the rest
Comparator | (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]) | (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1])
Interview tip: use Integer.compare rather than a[0] - b[0]; subtraction overflows when values are near the int limits (Minimum Arrows has such test cases).
Meeting Rooms II: min-heap of end times vs two sorted arrays vs TreeMap sweep

| Min-heap of end times | Sorted starts + sorted ends | TreeMap +1 / -1 sweep
Time | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n log n)
Extra space | O(n) | O(n) | O(n)
Can tell which room a meeting gets | Yes (store room ids) | No | No
Generalises to | Room assignment (Meeting Rooms III) | Max overlap count | Max overlap with weights (Car Pooling), "my calendar" queries
Rule of thumb: the heap version is the most common answer; the two-array version is shorter and shows you see it as "maximum overlap at any time".
Do touching intervals overlap? [1,2] and [2,3] in different problems

Problem | [1,2] and [2,3] | Condition to write
Merge Intervals | Merged into [1,3] | next.start <= cur.end
Meeting Rooms | No conflict (one ends as the other starts) | next.start < prev.end means conflict
Non-overlapping Intervals | Both can stay | keep if start >= lastEnd
Minimum Arrows (balloons) | One arrow at x = 2 bursts both | new arrow only if start > arrowPos
Interview tip: ask "do intervals that share an endpoint overlap?" before coding. Getting < vs <= wrong is the most common interval bug.
